statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-33116 (GHSA-37gx-xxp4-5rgx) is a .NET denial of service: a crafted document can drive the EncryptedXml class of System.Security.Cryptography.Xml into an infinite loop. Microsoft lists the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml package from 8.0.0 through 8.0.2 as affected and 8.0.3 as fixed, and the .NET 8.0.26 release ships System.Security.Cryptography.Xml 8.0.3 with the fix (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-37gx-xxp4-5rgx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/392, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.26/8.0.26.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. System.Security.Cryptography.Xml implementation code is in the ASP.NET Core shared framework (aspnetcore8-runtime), in the .NET SDK and its shared frameworks held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and in dotnet8-runtime-artifacts, which holds the ASP.NET Core runtime packs, internal transport packages and the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml NuGet package. In every build each of these copies is built from that build's own .NET release: 8.0.23, 8.0.24 and 8.0.25, with System.Security.Cryptography.Xml package 8.0.2, in the first three builds, and 8.0.26 or later, with package 8.0.3 or later, from 8.0.26-r0 on. dotnet8-runtime-artifacts also holds older System.Security.Cryptography.Xml versions (4.7.1, 6.0.1 and 7.0.1, and copies inside .NET build-tool packages) only as source-build reference assemblies, which carry no implementation code. The range ends at 8.0.26-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-33116 (GHSA-37gx-xxp4-5rgx) is a .NET denial of service issue in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml: crafted input can drive the EncryptedXml class into an infinite loop. Microsoft fixed the .NET 9 package in 9.0.15 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-37gx-xxp4-5rgx, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/392, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.15/9.0.15.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: System.Security.Cryptography.Xml.dll implementation assemblies ship in the ASP.NET Core shared framework in aspnetcore9-runtime, in the SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and in NuGet packages in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, and in every build they carry that build's .NET version; the aarch64 9.0.21-r0 build also holds an older 9.0.20 copy inside the Microsoft.DotNet.Arcade.Sdk package, which is still newer than the fix. The other copies are reference assemblies, which have no implementation. In 9.0.12-r0 through 9.0.14-r0 those implementation assemblies are 9.0.12 through 9.0.14, which are affected; from 9.0.15-r0 on, the version is 9.0.15 or later, with Microsoft's fix. The range ends at 9.0.15-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
